stem.text: Consider the differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} = - 3 y \sin{\left(x \right)} - 4 \). Decide whether it can be solved by separation of variables. If it can, write it with every factor involving y on the side of dy and every factor involving x on the side of dx; if it cannot, say so.

worked_solution.text: Separation needs \( - 3 y \sin{\left(x \right)} - 4 \) to be a function of x times a function of y. The term \( -4 \) contains no y and no factor \( \sin{\left(x \right)} \), so no such factorisation exists.
worked_solution.rule_named: test for a product of a function of x and a function of y

worked_solution.text: Equivalently, for \( F = - 3 y \sin{\left(x \right)} - 4 \) a product form would force \( F F_{xy} = F_x F_y \), which fails because the difference is \( 12 \cos{\left(x \right)} \). The equation cannot be separated.

options.label: \( \frac{dy}{y - 4} = - 3 \sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx \)
options.derivation: the constant treated as though it carried the factor - 3 \sin{\left(x \right)}, so the sum was factored falsely

options.label: \( dy = \left(- 3 y \sin{\left(x \right)} - 4\right)dx \)
options.derivation: dx moved across with y still on the side of dx, so nothing was separated

options.label: \( \frac{dy}{y} = \left(- 3 \sin{\left(x \right)} - 4\right)dx \)
options.derivation: the first term divided by y and the constant left beside it, as though the sum factored
